why: The last paragraph (EN and HI) says LIC earned Rs 13,492 crore in the April-June quarter, when profit had risen 22.8%. The verification notes admit IANS labels that figure Q1 FY26, which is April-June 2025, not 2026. The writer guessed it meant 2026, the LIC filing was never fetched, and the 22.8% has no source at all. The comparison may be wrong. Separately, the main picture is still the signboard of a small branch in Malbazar, West Bengal. It is close to a logo shot standing in for the country's largest insurer, and the hero brief asked for Yogakshema, the Mumbai headquarters.
